documents.title: Notification of transplant listing
documents.author: lung transplant
documents.body:
LUNG TRANSPLANT PROGRAM
Re: Lloyd Jacobs, DOB 10/26/1968

This is to notify you that as of 01/22/2026 your patient is active on the waiting list for bilateral lung transplantation for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. He has been instructed to keep his phone on at all times and to remain within travel distance of the center. He continues nintedanib and exertional oxygen through his pulmonologist while waiting.

Please let our coordinators know of any hospitalization, infection, new medication or vaccine while he is listed.

Lung Transplant Program

documents.title: Transplant discharge summary
documents.author: lung transplant
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - Lung Transplant Service
Admitted: 05/19/2026  Discharged: 06/02/2026

Admission diagnosis: idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, organ offer accepted.
Procedure: bilateral lung transplantation, 05/19/2026.

Hospital course: Called in overnight for a donor offer and taken to the operating room the same day. The operation was completed without complication. He was extubated early, transferred out of the ICU on schedule, and progressed steadily with physical therapy. Chest tubes were removed before discharge. The postoperative course was uneventful.

At discharge he is on room air, walking the unit independently.

Discharge medications:
- Tacrolimus 2 mg by mouth twice daily; goal trough 8-12 ng/mL, adjusted by the transplant team
- Mycophenolate mofetil 750 mg by mouth twice daily
- Prednisone 5 mg by mouth daily
Stopped: nintedanib. Home oxygen no longer needed.

Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: transplant clinic with frequent laboratory monitoring including tacrolimus levels; surveillance per program protocol. All medication changes go through the transplant team.

Lung Transplant Service

documents.title: Home
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted you to know I got the call in May and had the transplant. Home since the 2nd. Breathing without the oxygen for the first time in over a year. The transplant team is handling all my meds and labs, I have a binder the size of a phone book.

documents.title: Re: Home
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lloyd, this is wonderful news, thank you for telling me. We received your discharge summary last week. You're right to keep every medication question with the transplant team for now. I'm here for anything else, and we'll catch up in person once they give you the green light.

reports.text:
CHEST, PA AND LATERAL
Indication: fever, dyspnea and cough, 2 months after bilateral lung transplantation.
Comparison: none available at time of reading.
Findings: Postsurgical changes of bilateral lung transplantation. Diffuse interstitial infiltrates in both lungs. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal.
reports.conclusion: Diffuse interstitial infiltrates bilaterally after bilateral lung transplantation.

documents.title: Transplant pulmonary clinic note
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Transplant Pulmonary Clinic - copy to primary care
Date of service: 07/20/2026

Mr. Jacobs returns for scheduled follow-up of his IPF, now 2 months after bilateral lung transplantation, but today's visit is about two weeks of increasing breathlessness, a nonproductive cough and fevers. Recovery from surgery had been uneventful up to then. No sick contacts and no travel.

Medications: tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil and prednisone as at discharge.
Allergies: NKDA. Family history: father ILD, mother RA. Never smoker, 1-2 drinks/week before surgery, financial analyst.

Vitals: temperature 38.7 C (101.7 F), BP 130/85, heart rate 102, respiratory rate 26, SpO2 89% on room air.
Exam: crackles heard over both lungs.

Labs: WBC 9.0 K/uL, hemoglobin 12.5 g/dL, platelets 250 K/uL, creatinine 1.2 mg/dL, BUN 21 mg/dL, liver enzymes normal. CMV PCR positive.
Chest X-ray: diffuse interstitial infiltrates.

Impression: cytomegalovirus pneumonitis in a recent bilateral lung transplant recipient, with fever and hypoxemia.
Plan: direct admission to the transplant service today for IV ganciclovir and monitoring. Immunosuppression per inpatient team.

Transplant Pulmonary

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: lung transplant
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - Lung Transplant Service
Admitted: 07/20/2026 (direct from transplant clinic)  Discharged: 07/27/2026

Principal diagnosis: cytomegalovirus pneumonitis.
Background: bilateral lung transplantation 05/19/2026 for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.

Presentation: two weeks of dyspnea, dry cough and fever; in clinic 38.7 C, HR 102, RR 26, SpO2 89% on room air, bilateral crackles, diffuse interstitial infiltrates on chest film, CMV PCR positive.

Course: Started on IV ganciclovir 5 mg/kg every 12 hours on admission. Fever resolved and oxygen requirement fell over the following days. By discharge he was afebrile with SpO2 94% on room air. Transitioned to oral valganciclovir at treatment dose. Tacrolimus, mycophenolate and prednisone continued at the same doses.

Discharge medications:
- Valganciclovir 900 mg by mouth twice daily (new)
- Tacrolimus 2 mg by mouth twice daily, goal trough 8-12 ng/mL
- Mycophenolate mofetil 750 mg by mouth twice daily
- Prednisone 5 mg by mouth daily
Allergies: NKDA

Follow-up: transplant clinic in about 2 weeks; weekly CMV PCR and labs through the transplant program.

Lung Transplant Service

results.text: Detected, below the limit of quantitation

documents.title: Transplant clinic follow-up
documents.author: lung transplant
documents.body:
Lung Transplant Clinic - follow-up 08/13/2026

Seen 2.5 weeks after discharge for CMV pneumonitis. He feels much better, cough fading, no fevers at home. Afebrile in clinic, SpO2 95% on room air.
CMV PCR today: detected, below the limit of quantitation.

Plan: continue valganciclovir 900 mg twice daily with weekly CMV PCR until clearance, then the program will decide on the next step. Tacrolimus, mycophenolate and prednisone unchanged.

Lung Transplant Clinic

documents.title: Flu shot this year
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Getting my strength back after the CMV hospital stay. Question for the fall: am I still supposed to get a flu shot with all the transplant meds, and do I get it from you or from them?

documents.title: Re: Flu shot this year
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Good question. Yes, a flu shot is recommended, and it should be the regular injected kind (not the nasal spray). Transplant programs like to approve the timing, so please ask your coordinator when they want it. Once they okay it you're welcome to come here for it.
